sources.title: Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
sources.locator: Full 8-page PDF retrieved; inspected §I Eq. 1; §II Eqs. 2–9; §IV Eqs. 24–26 and focusing discussion at PDF pp. 4–5. The source uses hbar=c=1.

contents.name: §I Eq. 1 and §II Eqs. 2–9: total and transverse-projected angular operators, helicity basis, and gauge connection
contents.support: The review supplies operator and gauge context. The item uses the exact local helicity line and rotation suppliers, fixes the north-patch convention explicitly, and makes no global frame or classical-field identification.

contents.name: §IV Eqs. 24–26: ideal conical Bessel spin, orbital, and total labels
contents.support: The review motivates the sigma and cos(theta) correction. Its ideal delta-cone mode is not used as an L2 vector; the item proves the finite-width Hilbert-packet bound locally.

contents.name: §IV Eqs. 25–26 and focusing discussion: total angular momentum and helicity-preserving redirection
contents.support: The review motivates spin-to-orbit conversion in a stated optical model. The local proposition proves only the consequence of an explicitly assumed unitary Jz commutant and does not infer that a real focuser satisfies those assumptions.

sources.title: A. Bekshaev, M. Soskin, and M. Vasnetsov, Paraxial Light Beams with Angular Momentum
sources.locator: Full 87-page PDF retrieved; inspected §§2–3, PDF pp. 6–10, for the small diffraction-angle regime, azimuthal vortex modes, and the conventional beam SAM/OAM split; PDF pp. 26–27 for polarization conversion.

contents.name: §2, PDF pp. 6–7: paraxial propagation axis and small diffraction angle
contents.support: The review motivates an angular-cone definition. The local item replaces its beam-scale description by a precise Fourier-support cone and a specified north-patch photon helicity frame.

contents.name: §3, PDF pp. 8–10: conditional paraxial SAM/OAM separation and its convention warning
contents.support: The review's classical energy-flow split is treated as context only. The local result is proved for the bounded helicity-projected one-photon operator and does not identify it with a Poynting integral.

contents.name: Polarization-conversion discussion, PDF pp. 26–27
contents.support: The source describes one optical conversion model. It does not supply the general unitary domain-commutation hypothesis; the local proof states and uses that hypothesis explicitly.

sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6
sources.locator: Full author-hosted Chapter 6 HTML retrieved; §6.2.1 Eqs. 6.511–6.523 read in full; no paraxial estimate is attributed to these notes.

contents.name: §6.2.1 Eqs. 6.513–6.523: two transverse polarizations and the transverse projector
contents.support: The notes derive the momentum-space transverse plane and its projector and flag the lack of a global continuous polarization basis. The local item uses the already-defined complex helicity line and a local smooth gauge.

sources.title: Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
sources.locator: Full 8-page PDF retrieved; inspected §IV Eq. 24 gives the ideal conical Bessel spectrum and Eqs. 25–26 its angular-momentum labels; §II discusses the projected helicity operators.

contents.name: §IV Eq. 24: ideal delta-cone Bessel mode and its angular labels
contents.support: The paper supplies the limiting ideal mode as context. The example constructs a finite-bandwidth, finite-angular-width L2 vector and proves directly that an exact cone is null for the stated measure.

sources.title: A. Bekshaev, M. Soskin, and M. Vasnetsov, Paraxial Light Beams with Angular Momentum
sources.locator: Full 87-page PDF retrieved; inspected §§2–3, PDF pp. 6–10, and the vortex/polarization-conversion discussion at PDF pp. 26–27.

contents.name: §§2–3: paraxial vortex winding and conventional beam angular momentum
contents.support: The review motivates the integer azimuthal winding. The local packet is an exact transverse Hilbert vector; the review's classical beam decomposition is not imported as its proof.

sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6
sources.locator: Full author-hosted Chapter 6 HTML retrieved; §6.2.1 Eqs. 6.511–6.523 read in full; no paraxial estimate is attributed to these notes.

contents.name: §6.2.1 Eqs. 6.513–6.523: transverse photon modes and polarization completeness
contents.support: The notes provide QFT transverse-mode context. The finite-energy functional and vortex normalization are explicitly defined and proved in the local mathematical model.
